I'm looking for any advice anyone has to offer on how you manage your game assets?

In the past 13 years I have done only two files audits (last one in '09) and it has become a complete rats nest. I've decided enough is enough and myself and two lucky individuals (I chose at "random" ) are going to tackle this mess.

The problem is the 7 TB's of models, textures, source files, scripts, plans, books etc etc that are currently loosely organized into the projects from which they originated. The current system is driving everyone crazy, we've remade assets we already had and spent hours trying to find files. Also need to neatly archive outdated files. (can't delete them)

My plan is to go from project based to category based (example: Environment, Structures, Bio, Prop) and to create a full directory of all files that exist and their associated files (diffuse, normals, export prefs etc). Before we embark on this horrible journey, I'm looking for any advice. Does anyone have a special method they use? Maybe software to assist or a near perfect way of keeping track of files?

Don't be surprised when you have to write your own file management software for this. I've found it's rare to find assets that cleanly fit into any one category, even if they're only useful for one particular project. File formats that support in-file metadata (especially categorization/tagging data) are a godsend; sidecar files can be helpful but it's a pain to keep them moving with the original files themselves.

There are various useful asset management programs out there, but none that I've used enough to warrant mentioning. In any case, a centralized asset system will be very helpful once you get things organized.
